pages.text: In a $(item)Molten Salt Reactor$() the fuel is liquid: uranium fluoride dissolved in a lithium salt, pumped through a core of graphite. Graphite slows the neutrons; the salt carries the heat out.

A chain reaction holds steady when each fission leads to exactly one more: k = η f p ε, less what leaks out and what the boron $(thing)control rods$() absorb. Too little uranium and it will not go critical at all; too much and the rods must hold it back.

Salt expands as it warms, so k falls with temperature: the reactor finds its own temperature, where k is exactly one. Keep that between 732 K, where the salt freezes, and 980 K, where the vessel creeps. More fuel or fewer rods: hotter. More flow: more power at the same temperature.

The spent salt still holds most of its uranium, plutonium bred from uranium-238, and fission products. The cascade takes it apart by fluoride volatility: back to hexafluoride, plutonium and $(item)Fission Fragment Mix$(). Plutonium makes mixed-oxide fuel salt.
